description: Gemma 3 1B batch-1 prefill of 2048 tokens: where the q/k RMSNorm + RoPE kernels come from. TensorRT alone (the session recipe with CUDA graphs), the best hybrid with Inductor's kernels, the same q/k RMSNorm + RoPE regions with kernels written by PR 4914's KernelGenerator on the TensorRT-alone base, and the strongest Inductor configuration

notes.trt-session: The recipe the published agent session selected (not run by default). --session DIR replaces it with the recipe the session in DIR selected, and every TensorRT configuration here follows it
notes.trt-alone: TensorRT alone: the session recipe with runtime.cudagraphs, the base of the hybrid and generated configurations; TensorRT's own kernels run the q/k RMSNorm + RoPE
notes.trt-hybrid-rope-plugin: The best hybrid of the hybrid head-to-head: trt-alone with kernels.inductor set to the value the name gives
notes.trt-generated-qk-norm-rope: trt-alone with kernels.generated=qk-norm-rope: the q and k RMSNorm + RoPE of every layer as kernels PR 4914's KernelGenerator writes, hosted in the engine where rope-plugin hosts Inductor's kernels. Generated kernels come from the workload's kernel cache (its kernel_cache argument, else $TORCHTRT_KERNEL_CACHE, else the default directory), keyed by the region and the engine options; a build that finds none for its options generates them, so run the generated configuration once before timing it (bench_compare.py run, which has no time limit) or leave timeout_s room for the generator's 1800 s per distinct region, which it does
notes.inductor-fp16-fp16acc-max-autotune-torch: The strongest Inductor configuration of the hybrid head-to-head
